item.title: Thu Oct 29, 2026 — Midterms five days out: Democrats lead nationally, Senate map tightens in Texas, Ohio, Michigan
item.description: Midterms five days out: Democrats lead nationally, Senate map tightens in Texas, Ohio, Michigan · Fed holds rates as Warsh vows not to "waver" on inflation; 10-year yield tops 5% · Israel's election leaves no clear winner; Netanyahu bloc short of a majority · Big Tech earnings split: Microsoft beats on Azure, Alphabet slides on revenue miss
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Midterms five days out: Democrats lead nationally, Senate map tightens in Texas, Ohio, Michigan

Facts

  • RealClearPolling's national average has Democrats up 51.4% to 43.2%; a Reuters/Ipsos poll (Oct 22-26) shows Democrats ahead by nine points among all voters, per Al Jazeera's roundup.
  • Republicans hold 53 Senate seats; Democrats need a net gain of four for control and a net three seats to flip the House.
  • Texas: Democrat James Talarico leads Republican Ken Paxton 48.5% to 46.7% in the RCP average. Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed (D) vs. Mike Rogers (R) ranges from a 2-point to a 7-point Democratic edge depending on the poll.
  • Trump campaigned in Ohio for Sen. Jon Husted (vs. Sherrod Brown); Obama was in Georgia for Sen. Jon Ossoff; Vance rallied in North Carolina for Michael Whatley (vs. Roy Cooper). Trump heads to South Carolina, Florida and Kansas through Saturday.

Left view

Al Jazeera and CNN stress a national environment favoring Democrats, with new polls described as good news for Senate hopes. Reuters/Ipsos finds 73% of adults think the cost of living is heading the wrong direction and Trump's approval at 32%.

Right view

Fox News columnist Hugh Hewitt argues Republicans must unite behind Paxton despite frustration with the nominee, warning that losing the Senate would open the door to impeachment efforts and sap Trump's remaining agenda. Fox News's own forecast moved Texas from Lean R to toss-up. Note: I could not retrieve fresh National Review or Washington Examiner pieces today, so right-leaning coverage here is thinner than usual.

Watch for

Al Jazeera's analysis notes Democrats could win North Carolina and Ohio and still fall short of 51 seats, so Texas, Alaska and Kansas may decide control. A House-only flip would let Democrats block parts of Trump's agenda and open investigations. Early Georgia voting ends Friday; rural-vs-metro turnout (21% vs. 24% in Texas) is the tell Republicans are watching.

Sources: Al Jazeera Al Jazeera (Oct 28) CNN Fox News Mediaite

Fed holds rates as Warsh vows not to "waver" on inflation; 10-year yield tops 5%

Facts

  • The Fed left rates unchanged Wednesday. CNN's headline says two officials dissented in favor of a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh emphasized bringing inflation down and said incoming data will guide the December meeting.
  • The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.02%, crossing 5% (Motley Fool). The S&P 500 closed up 0.28% near 7,744.
  • This is a hawkish-leaning Fed: at the July meeting three officials also dissented for a hike, with the policy rate at 3.50%-3.75% (AP via KSL).

Left view

I did not retrieve a distinct left-leaning take today. Mainstream coverage (CNN) leads with the unusual hawkish dissents; the cost-of-living angle is central to Democrats' midterm message.

Right view

No fresh right-leaning commentary retrieved. In July, the Washington Examiner framed the hold as expected given "too-high inflation" it tied partly to energy costs from the Iran war. Treat that as background, not today's framing.

Watch for

Analysts quoted in July (Inflation Insights' Omair Sharif) expected hikes unless the labor market weakened sharply; others (Nationwide's Kathy Bostjancic) argued rate hikes cannot fix an energy supply shock. With yields above 5%, mortgage and corporate borrowing costs stay elevated. December is the next decision point.

Sources: Motley Fool CNN AP via KSL (July) Washington Examiner (July)

Israel's election leaves no clear winner; Netanyahu bloc short of a majority

Facts

  • With about 86% of votes counted, Netanyahu's right-wing/religious bloc has 53 seats, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's bloc 48, and predominantly Arab parties 19. A government needs 61 (Ynet).
  • Likud has 26 seats, Eisenkot's Yashar! 21, Naftali Bennett's Beyachad 12, and the Arab Joint List 13. Late-counted military and double-envelope ballots could still shift seats.
  • Israel may stay under a caretaker government while coalition talks run; Netanyahu assured Ben Gvir and Smotrich he will not abandon them (Times of Israel).

Left view

Eisenkot said voters chose change and urged Netanyahu to step down; the Democrats' Yair Golan urged the opposition to build a government with Arab-party support, and Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen said his party is ready to help remove Netanyahu (Ynet).

Right view

Netanyahu called on Zionist parties to unite and thanked coalition partners. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Trump does not want Ben Gvir and likely Smotrich in the next government. I did not retrieve Israeli right-wing outlets' own framing today.

Watch for

Final counts and certification next week, then President's consultations on who gets first shot at forming a government. A stalemate raises the odds of a long caretaker period, which matters for Iran decisions: military action needs government or security cabinet approval.

Sources: Ynet Times of Israel

Big Tech earnings split: Microsoft beats on Azure, Alphabet slides on revenue miss

Facts

  • After the close Wednesday, Microsoft topped expectations, led by Azure cloud; Alphabet shares fell after revenue came in below analyst forecasts (Motley Fool).
  • Earlier Wednesday, Oracle jumped 11% after an investor day and Vertiv rose nearly 17% on AI-infrastructure demand; F5 fell over 20% on weak guidance.

Left view

Not a story with a clear partisan split; I found no left-leaning commentary specific to today's earnings.

Right view

Likewise, no right-leaning commentary retrieved. Coverage is business-press only today (Motley Fool).

Watch for

Motley Fool expects tech volatility to return Thursday as investors judge megacaps on individual revenue results and whether heavy AI spending is paying off. With 10-year yields above 5%, high-multiple tech is sensitive to any hawkish rate repricing.

Sources: Motley Fool

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: +0.28% to ~7,744. Dow: +0.19% to ~52,475. Nasdaq: +0.27% to ~26,550 (Wed close, Motley Fool). Energy led; real estate and utilities lagged.
  • Rates: 10-year Treasury yield ~5.02%. Gold ~$4,068.
  • Oil: I could not verify a clean settle today. Reports in recent days put Brent well above $100 amid the Iran war and Hormuz disruption; one source says Iran claims Hormuz can reopen within days if the US lifts its blockade. Treat as unconfirmed.
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.23 per gallon, down from $4.27 a week ago and $4.41 on Oct 1.
  • Other: Reuters/Ipsos: 73% of US adults say cost of living is heading the wrong way.

Sports Watercooler

  • Baseball (bonus): Brewers led the World Series 3-0 after a 10-1 Game 3 rout of the Rays; Game 4 was Tuesday night in St. Petersburg. I could not confirm the Game 4 result.
  • Golf: No reliable results retrieved today.
  • Tennis: No reliable results retrieved today.
  • Squash: The PSA Tour is gearing up for the 2026-27 season; no specific results retrieved.
  • WWE: On Raw (Oct 26), Sami Zayn retained the Undisputed WWE Championship over Je'Von Evans after Bron Breakker interfered; John Cena returns to Raw next week in Brooklyn (early start, Netflix). Crown Jewel is Nov 7 in Riyadh.

item.title: Tue Oct 27, 2026 — DOJ charges Comey a third time, over a 2016 New York Times story
item.description: DOJ charges Comey a third time, over a 2016 New York Times story · US forces reportedly ready to hit Iran within 96 hours of an order; decision expected after the midterms · Midterms a week out: Democrats favored for the House, Senate in play · Anthropic files for a Nasdaq IPO, lifting tech stocks
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

DOJ charges Comey a third time, over a 2016 New York Times story

Facts

  • Prosecutors unsealed a two-count criminal information Monday accusing former FBI Director James Comey of transmitting, and conspiring to transmit, national defense information tied to an Oct. 5, 2016 New York Times article (Axios, Time).
  • The information was filed under seal Oct. 5. It skips a grand jury; the DOJ says it was filed to stop the statute of limitations from expiring while the investigation continues. Judge Trevor McFadden unsealed it but has not ruled on a motion to dismiss.
  • Two earlier cases: the false-statements indictment was dismissed in November 2025 over the prosecutor's appointment, and a case over the “86 47” post is set for trial in February 2027.
  • Separately Monday, a federal judge ruled that Comey's daughter Maurene, a former prosecutor, was unlawfully fired (Fox News).

Left view

Time and Axios stress that two prosecutor teams in Trump's first term declined to charge this same episode, that the filing appears to break the unofficial 60-day pre-election norm, and that Comey calls it persecution. The Times says such cases aim to chill sources.

Right view

Fox News presents it as the third matter against Comey and relays the DOJ position that filing an information to toll the statute of limitations is routine. Its coverage cited no Republican lawmakers; mainstream and right-leaning coverage of the legal merits was otherwise thin this morning.

Watch for

Whether McFadden accepts an information instead of an indictment; the limitations-period fight; whether prosecutors seek a grand jury before the Nov. 3 election. The statute-of-limitations dispute is the central legal question in the filings.

Sources: Axios Time Fox News

US forces reportedly ready to hit Iran within 96 hours of an order; decision expected after the midterms

Facts

  • CNN, citing two US officials, reports forces can launch a major operation within 96 hours of a presidential order; targets could include nuclear, military and energy sites. Trump has not decided, and officials say any order is more likely after Nov. 3.
  • Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials met Iranian leaders in Tehran, with Qatari mediation, to head off escalation in the eight-month war. Iran says it will reopen Hormuz if the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports; the US wants limits on enrichment.
  • Netanyahu reportedly asked for a joint strike before Israel's Oct. 27 election and Trump declined; his office denies this. The Houthis have attacked Saudi territory.
  • The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve is at its lowest level since 1982.

Left view

NPR's recent coverage emphasizes the economic fallout: jet fuel shortages, flight cuts and a nearly closed Hormuz. I did not retrieve a left-leaning take on the strike timing today.

Right view

Right-leaning framing, as in Fox News's Iran coverage, centers on Iranian attacks on shipping and mine-laying and on the blockade as leverage; Tehran's calls for a “single force” among Islamic nations get attention. I did not find a fresh right-leaning editorial on the strike timing today.

Watch for

Officials note Trump has appeared close to authorizing strikes before and backed off. Oil is the transmission channel: Brent is about $115 and WTI about $101, and Morgan Stanley is cited saying the fuel market stays tight through mid-2027.

Sources: Ynet / CNN report HNGN NPR Fox News

Midterms a week out: Democrats favored for the House, Senate in play

Facts

  • Election Day is Nov. 3. Democrats lead the generic ballot by about 9 points in Nate Silver's average and need a net three seats for the House (Yahoo News).
  • For the Senate, Democrats hold 47 seats and need four flips for 51. Polls show Democrats ahead in Maine, Ohio, North Carolina, Texas, Alaska and Michigan (D-held), with Iowa, Nebraska and Kansas close.
  • Trump's approval averages about 37% to 60% disapprove; on inflation and cost of living it is about 25% to 71%.
  • Redistricting in several Southern states may limit Democratic House gains.

Left view

The Yahoo News poll roundup frames it as Democratic momentum, with Trump's weak ratings on inflation and cost of living, and cautions that polls can be wrong. I did not retrieve a distinct left-leaning outlet take.

Right view

Fox News headlines say swing-state voters distrust the party they are backing and highlight Democratic criticism of Rep. Ilhan Omar days before the vote.

Watch for

Track the generic-ballot average and Senate toss-ups (Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas). Officials say any Iran strike order is more likely after Nov. 3.

Sources: Yahoo News Fox News

Anthropic files for a Nasdaq IPO, lifting tech stocks

Facts

  • Anthropic filed a prospectus with the SEC and plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. It had filed confidentially in June (TheStreet).
  • Earlier reports from the NYT and others put the target near a $2 trillion valuation and a raise above $100 billion; the prospectus terms were not confirmed in what I could read.
  • The news helped push the Nasdaq up 0.82% Monday as traders turned to a heavy big-tech earnings week.

Left view

I did not retrieve a left-leaning take on the filing today; coverage I saw was market-focused.

Right view

I did not retrieve a right-leaning take either; coverage was mostly market wires, so this story has no partisan split today.

Watch for

Pricing date and final valuation; whether Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon capex guidance this week supports the AI trade; supply effects of a very large listing on other tech stocks.

Sources: TheStreet Nasdaq.com

Fed meets today and tomorrow with inflation, not cuts, on the table

Facts

  • The FOMC meets Tuesday and Wednesday. Markets imply only about a 10% chance of a hike now, but traders watch Chair Kevin Warsh for signals on December (Capital.com via TheStreet).
  • Warsh has named October and December as decision points and signaled little tolerance for inflation above 2%.
  • The 10-year Treasury yield is about 4.98% and the 2-year about 4.71%.
  • Gas averages $4.29 a gallon, about 40% above a year ago.

Left view

No partisan commentary retrieved today; this is mainly a markets story.

Right view

No partisan commentary retrieved today; Warsh's own stated focus is holding inflation to 2%.

Watch for

A hold with hawkish language is the base case; a hike signal for December would pressure stocks and mortgage rates. Oil moves on Iran could change that math quickly.

Sources: TheStreet Kiplinger

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,676.80 (+0.70%). Dow: 52,361.52 (+0.28%). Nasdaq: 26,169.38 (+0.82%). Monday close, per TheStreet.
  • Oil: WTI fell 1.78% to $101.40 and Brent 1.34% to $115.20 on hopes of easing US-Iran tension; another report had Brent settling near $110.74.
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.2858, down about 20 cents from a month ago but up about $1.23 from a year ago.
  • Other: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report this week; 10-year yield about 4.98%.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Players keep leaving LIV, including Jon Rahm, Ian Poulter and Graeme McDowell, and Sergio Garcia has filed to end his contract; the DP World Tour reportedly plans a 2027 LIV ban (Golf Monthly). Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship.
  • Tennis: Basel round of 32 Monday: Casper Ruud, Holger Rune, Valentin Vacherot and Nuno Borges advanced (ATP).
  • Squash: I could not retrieve current PSA results this morning.
  • WWE: Raw from Fresno featured Becky Lynch vs. Stephanie Vaquer for a title shot at Liv Morgan, and Bayley vs. Lyra Valkyria in a No DQ match. I did not confirm results.
  • Hockey: Monday: Flames 5, Maple Leafs 2; Red Wings 4, Oilers 3 (SO); Kings 6, Rangers 3. Carolina leads the East with 20 points.
  • Soccer: Premier League Matchday 8: Arsenal won 2-0 at Everton, Liverpool 2-0 at Brighton, Aston Villa beat Man City 2-1, Bournemouth won 3-0 at Man United, and Tottenham won 2-0 at Chelsea.
  • Football: NFL Week 8 starts Thursday with Panthers vs. Packers.

item.title: Mon Oct 26, 2026 — Iran standoff: Trump weighs a deal or force as Qatari mediators reach Tehran
item.description: Iran standoff: Trump weighs a deal or force as Qatari mediators reach Tehran · Trump's DOJ moves into the midterm homestretch: Alaska certification suit, raids and indictments · Michigan Senate race: Trump and Obama campaign, with nine days to the midterms · Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Iran standoff: Trump weighs a deal or force as Qatari mediators reach Tehran

Facts

  • Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran on Sunday in an effort coordinated with Washington, per an official cited by Discovery Alert; Trump is reportedly weighing a negotiated arrangement against further military action.
  • Fox News (Oct 25) reports intelligence warning that Iran may be stepping up efforts to target Americans. Details of the intelligence were not published in what I could access.
  • Oil dipped on the diplomacy: WTI was near $101 and Brent near $114 early Monday, after nearly reaching six-month highs last week.
  • Hormuz disruption remains the key variable for physical oil flows.

Left view

Mainstream and left-leaning outlets were not retrievable today (NYT, WaPo, Guardian, MSNBC, Vox were blocked or stale), so I can't attribute a left framing. Axios, a center outlet, frames the Iran dip as diplomacy-driven positioning rather than restored supply.

Right view

Fox News's weekend panel framed Trump's choice as "make a deal or finish them off," leaning on the intelligence warning about plots against Americans.

Watch for

Vanda Insights' Vandana Hari expects volatile, upside-skewed oil risks, with possible strikes on Iran not ruled out after the Nov 3 midterms. JPMorgan sees Brent averaging about $87 in 2027 if the conflict is prolonged versus about $64 in a peaceful baseline. Goldman has modelled about 21 days of very low Hormuz flows followed by a slow recovery.

Sources: Discovery Alert Fox News Axios

Trump's DOJ moves into the midterm homestretch: Alaska certification suit, raids and indictments

Facts

  • Oct 23: DOJ sued preemptively to block certification of Alaska's Senate result if GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola, arguing a second candidate with a similar name could confuse voters. Alaska's Supreme Court previously ruled that candidate belongs on the ballot.
  • Trump said he ordered the suit. DOJ also sued California over ballots from suspected noncitizens, and agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's home on Oct 12.
  • Virginia state Sen. Louise Lucas was indicted Oct 22 and two former senior FBI officials were charged Oct 23 with lying to Congress over the Hunter Biden probe (per Axios).
  • Democrats and voting-rights groups have moved to intervene and asked a judge to dismiss the Alaska case (NBC News, CNBC).

Left view

Peltola called the suit "desperate" and spoke of "corruption" (The Hill, MS NOW headlines); Democracy Docket and MS NOW cast it as a bid to rig the Senate race. Axios notes legal experts questioned DOJ's authority to block certification of a state-run election and that the timing breaks the pre-election norm of restraint.

Right view

Trump: "I'm the one that said, 'Do it.'" DOJ says an unlawful ballot, once counted, "cannot be uncounted," and calls links to the midterms a smear. AG Todd Blanche said the Lucas probe began under Biden and that he works for Trump. Trump separately blasted Alaska's ranked-choice voting as "corrupt" (Washington Examiner).

Watch for

Court rulings on the Alaska case before Nov 3 and any post-election certification fights. Control of the Senate (53-47 GOP) could hinge on these races; Democrats need a net four seats.

Sources: Axios NBC News CNBC The Hill Democracy Docket Washington Examiner

Michigan Senate race: Trump and Obama campaign, with nine days to the midterms

Facts

  • Trump rallied in Port Huron backing Mike Rogers (Senate) and John James (governor) and called Democrat Abdul El-Sayed a "jihadist"; El-Sayed's campaign rejected the claim.
  • Obama campaigned in Detroit for El-Sayed and gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson; Bernie Sanders rallied for El-Sayed in Grand Rapids.
  • Republicans hold the Senate 53-47 and the House 218-214; Democrats need a net four seats in each chamber.
  • Trump floated a $5,000 "Trump dividend" if Republicans win both chambers (per Fox live coverage).

Left view

Sanders called Trump "mentally unbalanced" and El-Sayed's campaign calls Rogers a "rubber stamp" for Trump (as relayed by Fox News's live blog). Obama framed his pitch around a Democratic Party that can tolerate disagreement (Washington Examiner headline).

Right view

Speaker Mike Johnson dismissed recent polls as "wrong," citing a CNN report that October polls undersampled Republicans; Scalise called it a turnout contest. Notably, Rogers broke with Trump: "I've never called him a terrorist" (Washington Examiner).

Watch for

Turnout in Michigan and the Senate map decide chamber control. Analysts cited by Reuters (via Fox) lay out split-chamber outcomes as plausible.

Sources: Fox News live blog Washington Examiner Washington Examiner

Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil

Facts

  • Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff Sunday over Flavio Bolsonaro, son of Jair Bolsonaro, according to early results (Axios). The margin was not reported in what I could access.
  • Flavio Bolsonaro said he would not accept the result and called for it to be annulled, per translations cited by Axios.
  • The U.S. had imposed additional 25% tariffs on some Brazilian goods; Lula called Flavio "Trump's candidate" during the campaign.

Left view

Left-leaning outlets weren't retrievable today. Axios (center) characterizes the result as a setback for the right-wing populist movement and a counterweight to Trump's influence in Latin America.

Right view

Fox News led with "conservative wave hits roadblock," framing Lula as holding off the Bolsonaro challenge. No direct Trump reaction was reported in the sources I reached.

Watch for

Tariff tensions likely persist. Watch whether Flavio Bolsonaro's refusal to concede turns into protests or court challenges.

Sources: Axios Fox News

Israel votes Tuesday with Netanyahu's coalition trailing in final polls

Facts

  • Final polls from three major Israeli networks put Netanyahu's bloc near 50 of 120 seats, 17 fewer than his current coalition; Likud at about 20 versus 32 now.
  • Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc is projected at 52-56 seats; Arab parties at 14-16 combined. Pro-Netanyahu Channel 14 is the outlier, giving his bloc 60.
  • Netanyahu spoke with Trump twice in three days seeking more public backing, per Axios sources; Likud denied it. A U.S. official called it a "sign of desperation."

Left view

Mainstream and left outlets not retrievable today for attribution.

Right view

Fox News is running an Israeli surprise-attack drill story with an expert invoking 1973. Right-leaning framing of Netanyahu's request was not available beyond Likud's denial.

Watch for

A hung result could mean weeks of coalition talks, which matters for Iran policy and Gaza ceasefire arrangements. Watch for further Trump statements on the election.

Sources: Axios Fox News

Venezuela: Machado returns home; Serbia's ruling party falls

Facts

  • Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado made a surprise return to Venezuela after nearly a year abroad (Fox News, Washington Examiner), and Trump responded.
  • Washington Examiner's headline says doubts over democracy are deepening there.
  • Separately, Axios reports a student-led movement has toppled Serbia's longtime ruling party in an election (headline-level detail only).

Left view

Left-leaning coverage was not retrievable today.

Right view

Fox and the Washington Examiner both lead with Machado's return; the Examiner stresses lingering doubts about Venezuelan democracy.

Watch for

Whether Machado faces arrest or can organize; and whether Serbia's result forces a leadership change under President Vucic.

Sources: Fox News Washington Examiner Axios

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,623.68 (-0.52%). Dow: 52,215.16 (-1.23%). Nasdaq: 25,955.34 (-0.21%). Friday Oct 23 close (latest verified; per Tapeboard). Tech sector fell 2.82% and communication services 3.18%; energy led gains.
  • Oil: WTI closed Friday near $103.44 (+3.99%); early Monday WTI ~$101 and Brent ~$114 on Qatari mediation hopes (Discovery Alert).
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.2892 on Oct 25, about a cent lower on the week and roughly $1.23 (about 40%) above a year ago. AAA headline: crude nears $100 a barrel.
  • Other: 10-year Treasury yield 4.99%, VIX 19.45, gold $4,010. Axios says AI-related stocks are losing their market-moving power.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: John Catlin won the Hong Kong Open by five shots at 20-under 260 (Asian Tour, via Golf News Net). PGA Tour results were not retrievable today.
  • Tennis: Weekend results could not be verified today.
  • Squash: The Venus ABC Open (PSA Copper, Karachi) ran Oct 21-25; top seeds were Curtis Malik and Lucy Turmel. Final results not retrieved.
  • WWE: Crown Jewel still planned for Saudi Arabia on Nov 7 despite talent travel concerns. SmackDown build: Chelsea Green vs. Roxanne Perez for the women's title, and Giulia vs. Blake Monroe in a Street Fight (Sacnilk).
  • Hockey: No verified weekend scores were retrievable today.
  • Soccer: Premier League Sunday: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton, Man United 0-3 Bournemouth, Palace 0-2 Newcastle, Hull 1-1 Brentford, Sunderland 0-0 Leeds. Man City and Arsenal lead on 21 points (City ahead on goal difference).
  • Football: NFL Week 7: Seahawks 20, Chiefs 3 (Kansas City's first loss); Giants 27, Texans 21 (OT); Bengals 35, Ravens 13; Buccaneers 43, Panthers 13; Steelers 16, Saints 10 in Paris. Cowboys at Eagles on Monday night (ESPN).

item.title: Sun Oct 25, 2026 — US weighs new Iran strikes as Brent settles at $116.72, a five-month high
item.description: US weighs new Iran strikes as Brent settles at $116.72, a five-month high · Nine days out: Trump rallies in Georgia and Michigan as Fox polls show tight Senate races · Houthi missiles hit Saudi Arabia; Aramco pipeline flows jump to bypass Hormuz · West Bank lockdown, deadly Jordan church attack, and Israel's election Tuesday
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

US weighs new Iran strikes as Brent settles at $116.72, a five-month high

Facts

  • Brent crude settled at $116.72 on Friday (+3.1%), its highest close since April; WTI settled at $103.27. Brent was under $97 at the start of October (CBS News).
  • US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack said a strike on Iran could come this weekend; Trump has said any strikes would wait until after the Nov. 3 midterms, while also saying the US "may do another little Epic Fury" (CBS, Fox News).
  • Iran's armed forces chief said US warships will not be allowed in the Persian Gulf. Iran says it is open to talks under the June Pakistan-brokered interim deal but blames the continuing US naval blockade for the stall (CBS).
  • The Director of National Intelligence warned in a memo that Iran has stepped up efforts to target US personnel abroad; the State Department updated advisories for 14 countries and ordered non-essential staff out of Saudi Arabia.
  • Two supertankers reportedly hit mines on an unauthorized southern Hormuz route Friday, per the IRGC; Reuters reports Tehran has drawn up plans to damage Gulf undersea internet cables if strikes resume.

Left view

Left-leaning and international outlets (The Guardian, CBS live coverage, Slate) tie the escalation to household costs and the midterms, noting that Trump's own timeline puts action after Election Day and that UN Ambassador Mike Waltz has said the war could last another year.

Right view

Fox News emphasizes the pressure campaign: Treasury Secretary Bessent says Iranian oil revenue is being choked off, Kpler projects it could hit zero by mid-December, and Netanyahu says Trump told him the US is "ready to finish the job." Trump accused Iran of faking ship strikes to push up oil prices.

Watch for

Analysts quoted across outlets see crude staying elevated while Hormuz and Saudi infrastructure remain at risk; a strike before Nov. 3 would contradict Trump's stated timeline and could send oil sharply higher. Putin is due to host Iran's president in Moscow Oct. 27.

Sources: CBS News Fox News Gulf News

Nine days out: Trump rallies in Georgia and Michigan as Fox polls show tight Senate races

Facts

  • Trump cast an early ballot in Palm Beach, then rallied in Perry, Georgia, with a Port Huron, Michigan, stop planned Sunday. He announced a $4.2 billion Audi investment in Macon, Georgia.
  • Obama rallied in Cleveland (Amy Acton, Sherrod Brown) and Detroit (Abdul El-Sayed, Jocelyn Benson).
  • Fox News polls: Texas Senate tied at 49% (Paxton vs. Talarico); Ohio Brown 52%, Husted 47%; Maine Collins and Troy Jackson tied at 49%; Michigan El-Sayed 50%, Rogers 49% (Sept. 30).
  • Trump cut some agricultural tariffs on Canada after Sen. Susan Collins lobbied for farmer relief. In Ohio, Acton accused Republican Vivek Ramaswamy of exploiting her childhood abuse in an ad; Gov. DeWine urged its removal while Trump defended it.

Left view

Guardian and NPR coverage in recent weeks has framed the race as a referendum on Trump and the cost of living, with Democrats holding the edge; Obama's stops were aimed at turning out the base in Ohio and Michigan.

Right view

Fox News coverage stresses Republican strength in rallies and the economic announcements, and Mike Rogers is attacking El-Sayed as radical and alleging Muslim Brotherhood ties, which El-Sayed rejects. Trump mocked the crowd at Obama's Detroit event.

Watch for

Several Senate contests are within a point or two, so a handful of results could decide control. Voters' concerns about prices, oil and the Iran war could shift late-deciding voters; polls have missed in both directions before.

Sources: Fox News NPR

Houthi missiles hit Saudi Arabia; Aramco pipeline flows jump to bypass Hormuz

Facts

  • Saudi air defenses intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, Taif and Yanbu on Saturday; debris fell in the Mecca area, and the Houthis denied targeting Mecca or Medina.
  • CBS reports an earlier strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people, including one American; the airport planned to resume flights Sunday after a two-week closure. Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters Thursday.
  • Aramco's East-West pipeline flows, which bypass Hormuz, rose from 2 million to 7 million barrels per day. Air India and Akasa suspended Saudi flights into November.
  • Saudi, Pakistani, Egyptian and Turkish foreign ministers met their UK, French and German counterparts in Istanbul.

Left view

CBS and other mainstream live coverage treats the Houthi campaign as a direct consequence of the wider war that keeps oil prices high and puts US civilians at risk.

Right view

Fox News frames it as Iranian proxy aggression and highlights US assurances to Gulf partners and new sanctions on Iran's shadow fleet. Coverage of the Saudi front is thinner in right-leaning outlets than the Hormuz story.

Watch for

Damage to Saudi processing or export capacity is the biggest upside risk to crude beyond Hormuz, according to analysts cited in recent coverage. Watch whether the US widens its embassy drawdowns.

Sources: CBS News Gulf News

West Bank lockdown, deadly Jordan church attack, and Israel's election Tuesday

Facts

  • Netanyahu ordered a West Bank lockdown after two Israeli soldiers were killed near Hebron; Israeli forces killed two suspected gunmen (Fox News).
  • A gunman attack on a Christian funeral in Karak, Jordan, killed at least six according to the Jordanian government (Fox News), with other reports putting the toll at eight; Jordan declared three days of mourning. No group has claimed it.
  • Israel holds elections Tuesday, Oct. 27. Netanyahu said this week the Iranian regime must be overthrown.

Left view

Coverage from international and left-leaning outlets tends to center civilian impact and the election as a referendum on Netanyahu's war-time leadership.

Right view

Right-leaning outlets such as Fox emphasize security: the soldier killings, the closure of Hebron, and Netanyahu's argument that Iran is behind regional threats. I could not verify detailed framing from either camp today; coverage I reached was thin.

item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

US and Israel reportedly draft renewed Iran strikes for after Nov. 3; Hormuz attacks continue

Facts

  • The New York Times reports the US and Israel have drawn up plans to resume strikes on Iran after the Nov. 3 midterms, with possible targets including energy sites, nuclear facilities and missile and drone arsenals.
  • Trump says the US is "not negotiating" with Iran and that "something" will happen "fairly soon." He has also accused Iran of inventing "fake hits" and mines to push up oil prices before the election.
  • Iran's Revolutionary Guards say four oil-carrying vessels were hit and caught fire near Hormuz and three others struck mines, and warn US bases could be targeted if the US keeps escorting ships. An Iranian general said Tehran will not let US warships into the Persian Gulf.
  • CENTCOM marked 100 days of its naval blockade of Iranian ports, saying it has blocked at least $25 billion in crude exports. Talks are deadlocked.

Left view

Left-leaning and Democratic framing centers on cost and process: Slate and Fortune portray the war as a political and economic liability for Trump, and Democrats are using it to target Republican candidates, including some who never voted on it (Fortune, PolitiFact fact-checks the attacks). Democrats also say the president took the country into war without Congress and without thinking through the consequences (DCCC chair Suzan DelBene, via Fox News).

Right view

Fox News coverage stresses military results and resolve: Trump says the US has "knocked the hell out of" Iran, supporters quoted say high gas prices are worth preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon, and Fox contributor Rebeccah Heinrichs says strikes before the midterms are unlikely. The White House calls the price spike temporary. Netanyahu says the Iranian regime must be overthrown. Mainstream wire coverage and Israeli outlets add that the IDF chief reportedly sees no operational need to strike before the election.

Watch for

Analysts cited by market outlets see the post-election strike plan as an added oil risk premium: Brent closed at $116.72, its highest since late April. A strike on Iranian energy infrastructure or further mining of Hormuz would likely push crude higher; any back-channel deal would do the opposite. Iran's army chief says it is prepared for asymmetric warfare.

Sources: Times of Israel Fox News Slate Wall Street Republic

Gas at $4.30+, diesel above $6: the Iran war reaches household budgets

Facts

  • Regular gasoline averaged about $4.33 in mid-October, roughly 45% above the prewar $2.98, and AAA data cited by Slate and the Washington Examiner shows $4.30 to $4.37 this week. It is the first October with gas averaging above $4.
  • Diesel averaged about $6.33, up 68% from before the war, after a record $6.53 in September.
  • USDA now expects 2026 grocery prices up 2.4% (from 1.7%); airfares were up about 22% in September. Moody's Analytics estimates the war has cost the average household nearly $2,000.
  • The Strategic Petroleum Reserve is at its lowest in 44 years; the Department of Energy approved a further emergency exchange for a Phillips 66 refinery.

Left view

Slate argues gas prices may hurt Trump more than any other issue, citing a NYT/Siena survey of five red states in which voters disliked his handling of fuel prices most, and noting his earlier pledge of sub-$2 gasoline. Democrats call the prices "another broken promise" (DelBene).

Right view

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt says the surge is temporary and prices "will plummet" once Operation Epic Fury ends. The NRCC's Richard Hudson points to the tax law's no-tax-on-tips and overtime provisions. The Washington Examiner reports that the war and gas prices have undercut the GOP's tax-cut pitch, a candid acknowledgment from a right-leaning outlet.

Watch for

Cornell economist Chris Barrett sees "very little prospect" of a significant fuel price drop soon; AFS Logistics expects fuel to keep transport costs elevated. Wells Fargo warns diesel costs will squeeze discount retailers, and the EIA projects heating oil 21% higher this winter.

Sources: Denver Gazette Washington Examiner Fox News

Eleven days out, polls favor Democrats; early vote tops 20 million

Facts

  • The Silver Bulletin generic-ballot average has Democrats up 8.6 points (49.7% to 41.1%); NYT/Siena in September had it 51% to 43%. Trump's approval average is about 36%.
  • Senate polling cited by Forbes: Texas tied (Talarico and Paxton 49% each, Fox News poll), North Carolina Cooper +10, Georgia Ossoff +8, Ohio Brown +5, Michigan El-Sayed +2, Maine Jackson +2 over Collins. Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority.
  • Prediction markets (Kalshi) give Democrats about a 90% chance of winning the House. Early voting has passed 20 million ballots.

Left view

Outlets such as Slate and Fortune frame the race as a referendum on the war and prices, with Democrats pressing affordability. Democrats also say they plan investigations into the administration if they win a chamber (per Forbes).

Right view

Republican messaging, per the Washington Examiner and Fox, leans on the tax law and argues price pain is tied to a war the White House says will end. Trump has said the midterms carry "a price to pay" but defends the Iran campaign. Right-leaning outlets also highlight Democratic controversies, such as renewed scrutiny of Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's ties to a streamer who made inflammatory remarks about the US.

Watch for

Forecasters note that Texas, Iowa, Kansas and Maine are within a couple of points, so a few results could decide Senate control. Several Republicans-leaning analysts caution that polls have missed in both directions before. Another factor is whether Iran escalation before Nov. 3 shifts turnout.

Sources: Forbes Rio Times PolitiFact

Gulf spillover: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, tanker spill off the UAE

Facts

  • An attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed at least one person (later reported as two) and injured eight, per Saudi authorities. The State Department ordered non-emergency US personnel and families to leave Saudi Arabia; the order does not cover the wider Gulf.
  • The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh. Houthi health authorities blamed Saudi airstrikes for civilian deaths near Taiz and at a migrant shelter in Saada; Saudi Arabia did not comment.
  • Beaches in Umm Al Quwain, UAE, were closed after a tanker oil spill; authorities say there is no health risk.

Left view

Left-leaning coverage (Slate, Fortune) treats Houthi pressure on Saudi refineries as another consequence of the war that keeps oil prices elevated. Saudi Arabia produces about 11% of global supply.

Right view

Fox News live coverage frames the escalation as Iranian proxy aggression and highlights US assurances to Qatar and freedom of navigation, alongside new Treasury and allied sanctions on Iran's shadow shipping fleet. Right-leaning outlets are leading on the sanctions angle; mainstream coverage here is thinner.

Watch for

Analysts say damage to Saudi processing or export capacity would be the biggest upside risk to crude beyond Hormuz. A wider US drawdown from Gulf posts would signal expectations of escalation.

Sources: AP via Netscape Fox News

West Bank lockdown in Hebron, deadly church attack in Jordan, Gaza deal stalled

Facts

  • Israel closed all entrances and roads into Hebron and forced residents from homes after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers; up to 300 families left Deir Baha, per the municipality.
  • The death toll from a gunman's attack on a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, rose to eight; more than two dozen remain hospitalized.
  • Haaretz reports Israeli military intelligence told the US that Hamas does not intend to disarm and has 30,000 to 40,000 operatives. US-led efforts for a disarmament-for-withdrawal deal have stalled. Gaza's health ministry says more than 1,500 Palestinians have died since the October 2025 ceasefire.

Left view

Left-leaning and international outlets emphasize civilian harm and settler conduct: reports from the olive harvest describe settlers confronting farmers, and over 70 activists were detained, with four Americans released with exclusion orders.

Right view

Israeli government framing, echoed in right-leaning outlets, stresses security: Defense Minister Israel Katz blamed opposition leaders for criticism of security warnings (Lapid and Eisenkot condemned the remarks), and the Hamas-rearmament intelligence supports calls to keep military pressure. Netanyahu ties the regional threat to Iran.

Watch for

Analysts expect further West Bank closures and a possible Israeli response in Gaza if the disarmament track collapses. The UAE's nomination of Lana Nusseibeh for UN secretary-general could shift diplomacy at the Security Council.

Sources: AP via Netscape Times of Israel

Markets & Economy

  • Friday close: Dow: -1.23% (about -653 pts). S&P 500: -0.52% (about -40). Nasdaq: -0.21% (about -54). S&P is up about 11.4% year to date; breadth weak and sentiment in "Extreme Fear" for over a week.
  • Oil: Brent settled at $116.72 (+3.1%), highest close since late April; WTI $103.27 (+3.8%). Exxon, Chevron and ConocoPhillips closed at record highs.
  • Gas: national average about $4.30 to $4.37 (AAA, per Examiner and Slate); diesel above $6.
  • Rates: 10-year Treasury yield about 5.00%. The Fed decides Oct. 28: CME FedWatch shows roughly 80% to 91% odds of a hold at 3.75%-4.00%, with a hike expected by Dec. 9 per Forbes. Chair Kevin Warsh presides.
  • Other: AT&T fell 8% and T-Mobile 7.7% on a Bloomberg report that SpaceX is in talks to access tower sites; Crown Castle rose 9%. CrowdStrike +8.3%, Palo Alto +7.2%. Dollar General and Dollar Tree fell over 4% on diesel-cost worries (Wells Fargo).

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: At the PGA Tour's Butterfield Bermuda Championship, Chandler Blanchet led at 9 under early in the event (two eagles Thursday), with Corey Conners a shot back after a 63; check final-round standings. On the LPGA, Haeran Ryu leads the BMW Ladies Championship by two after a second-round 64.

  • WWE: SmackDown: Chelsea Green retained the Women's title over Roxanne Perez; Blake Monroe beat Giulia in a Street Fight; Michin and B-Fab won the Women's Tag titles. Next week: Trick Williams vs. Sami Zayn for the Undisputed title. Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton is set for Crown Jewel, and CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens in Brooklyn in two weeks.
  • Hockey: Canadiens 4, Blackhawks 1 (Evans two goals; Suzuki out 2-4 weeks). Thursday: Maple Leafs edged Rangers on a late Stecher goal, and Oilers beat Hurricanes in a shootout (McDavid and Draisaitl five points each). Saturday slate includes Leafs-Oilers and Red Wings-Flames.

The Big Stories Today

US orders diplomats out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate

Facts

  • The State Department ordered non-emergency US government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia (CBS News). Spokesperson Tommy Pigott said the Iran-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against the kingdom.
  • Houthi strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport on Oct. 10 killed 12 and injured more than 300, including one American (CBS). An AFP tally cited by Gulf News puts deaths at Saudi airports this month at 22.
  • Aramco told Dhahran HQ staff to work remotely; debris from an intercepted drone killed two near the Shaybah oilfield (Gulf News, CBS). The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade near Bab al-Mandab, and the US military is quietly trimming its regional footprint (CBS).
  • Trump did not rule out striking the Houthis (“We may”) and has floated asking Turkey's Erdogan to help (Times of Israel/Reuters). Britain is adding RAF Typhoon patrols; Egypt pledged support.

Left view

Democratic framing wasn't retrievable today. The one documented Democratic voice on adjacent issues is House leader Hakeem Jeffries, who has accused the administration of overreach at home (see Omar story); on the Gulf, expect questions about another open-ended Middle East commitment and congressional authorization. Treat as unverified: no left-leaning outlet piece on this was retrieved.

Right view

Fox News is running a live blog tying the Houthi escalation to the broader Iran war and to Trump's threats of military punishment. The right-of-center case generally stresses deterrence and backing Saudi Arabia. I could not retrieve the commentary itself, so this is a description of coverage, not a quoted take.

Watch for

Whether Washington moves from evacuation to strikes; Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab shipping disruption on top of the Hormuz disruptions already tied to the US-Iran war (CBS). Oil hit a five-month high Thursday (see Markets). Analysts quoted by Gulf News flag whether Saudi air defenses can protect airports and energy sites as the key variable.

Sources: CBS News Gulf News Times of Israel Al Jazeera Fox News

Trump approval hits a record-low 31% with midterms 11 days away

Facts

  • Reuters/Ipsos (poll closed Oct. 19; 1,679 adults) has Trump at 31%, the lowest of either term and down a point in two weeks.
  • Among registered voters, Democrats lead the generic ballot 47%–35%, the widest gap of this cycle. Margin of error is 2 points (3 for registered voters).
  • Reuters ties the mood partly to worry over high gasoline prices. Midterms are Nov. 3.
  • Caveat: national generic-ballot numbers don't capture district-level maps, where Republicans keep some structural advantages (Reuters).

Left view

Democratic-aligned commentary reads the poll as a referendum on prices and the Iran war. Political Wire relays Charlie Cook's view that Republicans' structural advantages have “evaporated” and the midterms are heading somewhere “very grim” for the GOP. (Cook is a nonpartisan handicapper, not a left outlet.)

Right view

No right-leaning outlet response was retrieved. The usual counter is that single polls overstate swings and that district maps and turnout, not national approval, decide House and Senate control; Reuters itself notes the structural-advantage caveat.

Watch for

Final-week spending and “October surprises” (Democrats are wary after the Omar search); whether gas prices ease before Nov. 3; Cook Political Report rating shifts toward Democrats in several governor races.

Sources: Reuters/Ipsos via The Star Political Wire

Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's home weeks before the election

Facts

  • Homeland Security investigators searched Omar's Washington home on Oct. 12 under a federal warrant, part of what the Justice Department calls a criminal investigation (AP via local stations; ITV).
  • Details are sparse. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin has previously cited an ongoing probe into possible fraud tied to her family's immigration paperwork (ITV).
  • Trump deferred to DOJ (“that has nothing to do with me”) but called Omar “very crooked.” DOJ practice has long been to avoid actions touching candidates close to elections (ITV).

Left view

Jeffries and congressional Democrats said Trump and “far-right extremists” have relentlessly targeted Omar and that the administration's “violent mass deportation machine” entered a sitting member's home. Omar called it an attempt to weaponize law enforcement against political enemies.

Right view

No right-leaning outlet text retrieved. The administration's position, via Trump and DHS, is that this is an ordinary law-enforcement matter run by DOJ, not a political one.

Watch for

Whether charges follow and how the warrant's basis becomes public; whether the timing reshapes Minnesota and national midterm messaging; any DOJ internal pushback on pre-election timing.

Sources: ITV News AP via KSAT Al Jazeera Boston Globe

Gas near record-for-season highs as the Fed edges toward hikes

Facts

  • AAA's page shows a national average of about $4.29 as of Oct. 23, down from $4.41 on Oct. 1 and up from $3.16 a year earlier (the AAA page's own date labels conflict, so treat the exact figure as approximate). September averaged $4.33, a record for the month.
  • AAA says prices are the highest ever for this time of year. California leads at about $6.40.
  • Crude fell back toward $90 at points in late September/early October but hit a five-month high Thursday after the Houthi strikes (GV Wire/AP-style wire).
  • Markets are pricing a likely 25-basis-point Fed hike by year-end; Barclays expects hikes in December and January (Reuters via Kitco).

Left view

No left-leaning outlet piece retrieved. Democrats' general message, as reflected in polling coverage, ties pump prices to the Iran war and Trump's policies.

Right view

No right-leaning outlet piece retrieved. The administration's counter-argument is typically that supply disruption originates with Iran and its proxies, not domestic policy.

Watch for

Oil path depends on Red Sea and Hormuz traffic. Higher fuel costs are already showing in earnings (Union Pacific flagged them; P&G warned of cost pressure). A hike would hit housing and equity valuations; the 10-year yield was 5.10% on Oct. 15.

Sources: AAA Reuters via Kitco GV Wire

AI spending fears hammer chip and megacap stocks

Facts

  • Thursday's chip rout dragged the Nasdaq to its worst day since early June. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 6.3%, its biggest drop since June 23.
  • Meta fell 7.5% despite beating expectations, after reporting its first cash outflow in over a decade and announcing a stock split plus non-voting shares to fund AI spending. Tesla slipped 2.1%.
  • Analysts cited doubts about AI returns, regulatory risk, and higher-for-longer rates and oil (GV Wire). Last week CoreWeave bonds sold off with yields above 15% (Reuters via Kitco).
  • Winners included Spotify (+10.7%), Procter & Gamble (+6.0%) and Lockheed Martin (+6.1%).

Left view

No left-leaning outlet take retrieved. Progressive coverage of AI tends to emphasize concentrated financing risk and political backlash, which one analyst also named as a driver.

Right view

No right-leaning outlet take retrieved. Market-oriented commentary generally frames this as a valuation reset after a long run (S&P up roughly 13% YTD as of Oct. 15), with defense and consumer staples acting as havens.

Watch for

More AI-linked earnings and financing deals; whether a reported lower valuation for Anthropic's planned IPO becomes a sentiment marker (Reuters mention); Fed-hike pricing.

Sources: GV Wire Reuters via Kitco Tapeboard

Markets & Economy

item.title: Thu Oct 22, 2026 — US pulls non-emergency staff from Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
item.description: US pulls non-emergency staff from Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate · Iran war: talks "continue," but Hormuz stays shut · Midterms, 12 days out: Senate debates, Trump on the trail, Omar raid fallout · Russia frees an American as US–Ukraine ties stay strained
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

US pulls non-emergency staff from Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate

Facts

  • The State Department ordered non-emergency US government employees and their families out of Saudi Arabia on Wednesday; a spokesperson said the order covers Saudi Arabia only, not the wider Gulf.
  • Saudi authorities say an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one and injured eight, and a drone strike on an Aramco facility at Shaybah killed two. Earlier this month a strike on Riyadh's King Khalid airport killed at least 13 and wounded more than 300.
  • ACLED data cited by Fox News show Houthi strikes and attempted strikes more than doubled in one week this month. Riyadh has asked Washington for more missile interceptors; Rubio said global demand is very high and the US must balance allies' requests against its own needs.
  • Trump said of direct strikes on the Houthis, "We may. We're gonna look at it." Britain is sending Typhoon jets to defend Saudi cities; Egypt is helping and Israel has offered help.
  • Brent crude rose about 1.2% to roughly $110 in early Asian trading Thursday on the news.

Left view

I could not retrieve a left-leaning outlet's take on the evacuation today. Earlier CBS News coverage of the war has carried criticism from Gold Star family members who called the administration "reckless" with service members' lives, and the interceptor shortage ties into the broader left critique that the war is stretching US stockpiles. Treat this framing as thin.

Right view

Fox News leads with the evacuation as Trump "weighs his next move" on the Houthis, and its live blog carries Trump's claim that the US has "decimated" Iran and that high gas prices are a "small price to pay" to stop an Iranian nuclear weapon. Mainstream wire and business outlets (Bloomberg, Global News) report the same facts with less emphasis on Trump's rhetoric.

Watch for

Analysts quoted around the story point to risk for Gulf oil infrastructure and aviation if Houthi strikes keep widening. Watch for a decision on US strikes in Yemen, more allied air-defense deployments, and whether the order expands beyond Saudi Arabia. Another round of attacks on Saudi energy sites would push Brent higher.

Sources: Fox News Fox News live blog Global News Bloomberg Arab News

Iran war: talks "continue," but Hormuz stays shut

Facts

  • Foreign Minister Araghchi says negotiations with the US continue through Qatari and Pakistani mediators, that Hormuz "remains closed," and that Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait on day six of an agreement if the US accepts its conditions (Israel Hayom, citing an Iraqi-media interview).
  • Iran says the US must first commit to the "Islamabad memorandum of understanding." Security council secretary Rezaei said Tuesday no enriched uranium will leave Iran; President Pezeshkian wants sanctions lifted before dialogue.
  • The IRGC on Wednesday threatened to cut undersea data cables in the strait. The IMO says mines remain a serious threat and cannot be verified as cleared; two tankers hit mines Oct. 17.
  • Trump has said the US won't attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterms, and that the US "could leave now" but wants its gains to last. WTI settled near $97 Wednesday; Brent is near $110.

Left view

The Atlantic reported earlier this month that the White House asked the Pentagon for strike options before the midterms, which critics read as electoral calculation. CBS News has carried Gold Star family members' demands for transparency. Left-leaning analysis, like Al Jazeera's midterm piece yesterday, ties the war to gas prices and Trump's approval slide.

Right view

The Washington Examiner (opinion, Oct. 17) describes the conflict as a "staring contest over a strait" that did not end in unconditional surrender but will shape the midterms. Fox News stresses Trump's firmness and the damage done to Iran, plus Iran's hardline terms. Not all conservatives are comfortable with the gas-price cost.

Watch for

If the Qatar-Pakistan channel produces a deal, expect a sharp oil drop; without one, markets are pricing a prolonged closure. Watch Iran's response on the seven-day plan, further mine or tanker incidents, and any shift in US posture after Nov. 3.

Sources: Israel Hayom Arab News Pakistan Fox News live blog CBS News Washington Examiner

Midterms, 12 days out: Senate debates, Trump on the trail, Omar raid fallout

Facts

  • Fox News reports Michigan Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed (D) and Mike Rogers (R) debated; El-Sayed spent much of it attacking Rogers until Rogers broke with him on a policy issue. CNN's midterm live blog headline says Republicans in the Michigan and Kansas debates made careful breaks with Trump (I could not open the article).
  • Fox News says Trump halted a South Carolina rally after a scuffle broke out in the crowd; I could not find a second source with details.
  • Rep. Ilhan Omar said the federal raid on her home was meant to intimidate voters, per Fox News.
  • A Fox News poll indicates a key voting bloc's shift could decide the Texas Senate race. Yesterday's Reuters/Ipsos poll put Trump's approval near 31% and Democrats up 47–35 on the generic ballot. Election Day is Nov. 3.

Left view

Left-leaning outlets frame the Omar raid as political intimidation (Common Dreams and The Nation both ran critical pieces on it). Al Jazeera's debate takeaways and CNN's live blog emphasize Republicans distancing themselves from Trump on the war and costs.

Right view

Fox News covers the Michigan debate through El-Sayed's attacks on Rogers and treats the Omar story as a response to long-running rumors about her; the Fox/Texas poll framing is that the race is competitive and winnable. Conservative coverage is largely not disputing the poll numbers, but stressing turnout and spending.

Watch for

Analysts point to turnout and late-deciding blocs rather than shifts in national sentiment. Watch Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas and Kansas, the war's effect on gas prices before Nov. 3, and whether more Republicans separate from Trump on Iran.

Sources: Fox News CNN live blog Al Jazeera Common Dreams The Nation

Russia frees an American as US–Ukraine ties stay strained

Facts

  • Fox News reports Russia freed an American teacher held on Ukraine mercenary charges after Trump pressed Putin. I could not find the name or a second source today.
  • Yesterday's AP reporting described US–Ukraine relations at a new low after Trump rejected new Russia sanctions and said "maybe it's time" for Zelenskyy to get another negotiator; the Washington Post reported Hegseth withheld approval for some weapons transfers.
  • Rubio said "nothing has changed" and the Pentagon is prioritizing US stockpile needs.

Left view

AP and NPR (yesterday) framed the administration's moves as Russia-friendly and potentially tipping the war toward Moscow; left commentary points to the sanctions waiver and the interceptor shortage. Today I did not retrieve a left-leaning take on the prisoner release itself.

Right view

Fox News presents the release as a result of Trump's direct pressure on Putin. The administration line is burden-sharing and a push for a negotiated end. I did not retrieve a National Review or Free Press piece, so this side is thinly sourced.

Watch for

Analysts have warned of an interceptor gap as winter strikes on Ukrainian cities begin. Watch whether the release leads to broader US–Russia talks, and whether Congress moves sanctions legislation.

Sources: Fox News AP NPR

AI trade wobbles: Meta, Tesla earnings after SpaceX pops

Facts

  • Wednesday's close: S&P 500 7,757.17 (+0.58%), Dow 52,856.09 (+0.69%), Nasdaq 26,702.86 (+1.05%). SpaceX (SPCX) rose about 10% after beating forecasts on AI-business growth.

item.title: Wed Oct 21, 2026 — Trump's approval hits a record low as midterms close in
item.description: Trump's approval hits a record low as midterms close in · Iran war: stalemate on talks, Hormuz still disrupted · US-Ukraine ties hit a new low · France imposes curfews after violent weekend protests
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Trump's approval hits a record low as midterms close in

Facts

  • A Reuters/Ipsos poll puts Trump's approval at about 31%, the lowest of either term, down from 32% two weeks ago.
  • On the generic ballot Democrats lead 47%–35%, a 12-point gap that is the widest of the cycle (1,679 adults surveyed).
  • Republicans hold the House 218–214 and the Senate 53–47. Federal News Network's piece on Kalshi pricing puts Democratic Senate-control odds in the mid-60s; that article was sponsored content.
  • Money is flooding in: Trump says he'll spend over $400M for GOP candidates, Reuters reports Elon Musk has put in about $366M, and the NYT reports Bloomberg is giving Democrats $80M for the House. Cook rates seven Senate races as toss-ups (AK, IA, KS, ME, MI, OH, TX).
  • Election Day is Nov. 3. Trump was in Kansas Monday and North Carolina Tuesday.

Left view

Al Jazeera's analysis ties the slide to the unpopular Iran war and high living costs, and cites researchers who say Republicans have very small odds of keeping their narrow majorities. Historical data cited: the governing party lost House seats in 18 of the last 20 midterms.

Right view

Townhall (conservative) leads with Trump's $400M-plus spending as a patriotic push and quotes his "Edge of Oblivion" framing, with little on the polling. Treasury Secretary Bessent argued a Democratic Congress could do little to stop the Trump agenda (via a syndicated report). Caveat: right-leaning outlets are not disputing the numbers so much as stressing the money and turnout; I did not find a major conservative rebuttal of the poll today.

Watch for

Experts note exit polls have run slightly more favorable to presidents than pre-election polls, so turnout may matter as much as sentiment. A Democratic Senate flip would need a net gain of four seats; watch Maine, Texas (Talarico vs. Cruz), Michigan and Ohio.

Sources: Al Jazeera Federal News Network Townhall AP

Iran war: stalemate on talks, Hormuz still disrupted

Facts

  • The war began in late February with joint US-Israeli strikes and is now about eight months old. A US naval blockade remains in place.
  • Iran says it won't negotiate until the US lifts sanctions and ends pressure, and an Iranian security official said no enriched uranium will leave the country. Iran's foreign minister said Hormuz stays closed until the US accepts Iran's terms.
  • Qatar and Pakistan are reportedly brokering a compromise (interest on $6B in frozen Qatari-held funds in exchange for an IAEA visit); the report says the US approved and Iran responded positively, with a breakthrough possible this week. That comes from sourced reporting, not an official announcement.
  • The White House says the US won't attack Iran before the midterms; Trump has floated resuming strikes afterward. Mines reportedly disabled three tankers, and UKMTO says October is the worst month for shipping attacks since March.
  • Lavrov visited Tehran, his first trip since the war began; Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Israel, where Netanyahu said "we have a job to finish."

Left view

CBS's live coverage and the Detroit News (USA Today network) carry officials' claims that Iran is deliberately prolonging talks to influence US midterms, alongside Iranian statements blaming US "warmongering." Critics on the left tie the war to rising gas prices and the president's slump, as in Al Jazeera's midterm analysis.

Right view

Fox News' live blog leads with Iran's "hardening" terms and Iranian attacks on shipping, and presents Trump, Rubio (who compared Iranian tactics to "Nazi U-boat tactics") and CENTCOM as firm. Not every conservative is cheering: Lara Trump has reportedly said the war could cost the GOP the midterms over gas prices.

Watch for

If the Qatar-Pakistan channel works, expect a quick oil drop; if not, markets are pricing a long closure. Brent hit its highest since mid-May on Tuesday. Watch the Oct. 26 Egyptian parliament vote on military support for Saudi Arabia and any escalation after Nov. 3.

Sources: CBS News Fox News Detroit News The National

US-Ukraine ties hit a new low

Facts

  • AP reports relations are at a new low after more than a week of Trump insulting Zelenskyy, rejecting new Russia sanctions and easing up on Moscow.
  • Trump said "maybe it's time" for Zelenskyy to get somebody else to negotiate for Kyiv.
  • The Washington Post reported Defense Secretary Hegseth has withheld approval for some weapons transfers to Ukraine; satellite-support disruptions have also hurt Ukraine's drone use. Zelenskyy says Ukraine lacks enough missile interceptors and that he feels betrayed.
  • Rubio said "nothing has changed," called the reports inaccurate, and said the Pentagon is prioritizing US stockpile needs, including NATO commitments. He did not dispute the interceptor shortage.
  • AP reports bipartisan lawmaker outrage.

Left view

NPR frames the moves as "Russia-friendly" steps as Trump looks for a way to end the war, and AP's framing is that the policy shift could tip the war toward Russia. Left-leaning commentary emphasizes the sanctions waiver and interceptor shortage as concrete harm to Ukraine.

Right view

The administration's line (Rubio) is that US policy is unchanged and that arms reach Ukraine through European purchases, with US stockpile needs coming first. Fox hosts and some conservative voices frame it as burden-sharing and a push for a negotiated end; I did not retrieve a National Review or Free Press piece today, so treat this characterization as thinner than the left-side sourcing.

Watch for

Analysts warn a gap in interceptors heading into winter strikes on Ukrainian cities, and that a Trump push for new negotiators could split Kyiv and Europe from Washington. Watch Congress for sanctions legislation and any Pentagon clarification on the held-up weapons.

Sources: AP NPR ABC Australia Fox News

France imposes curfews after violent weekend protests

Facts

  • After weekend protests turned violent, with riots and looting, curfews were expanded beyond Paris to Nice, Lyon and parts of the Gironde.
  • PM Lecornu called for partial curfews through regional authorities; Macron declined a minister's resignation and is on a Gulf trip. CNBC reports the curfews have calmed unrest.
  • I could not retrieve the full articles today, so the underlying trigger of the protests is not detailed here.

Left view

Coverage I could access (Al Jazeera, Euronews) centers on the government's response and political fallout for Macron; no distinct left-wing framing was retrieved.

Right view

Fox News' Iran analyst Lisa Daftari called the unrest "organized lawlessness" and linked it to broader Iranian influence, a claim I could not verify independently.

Watch for

Watch whether curfews hold through the week and whether the unrest becomes a larger test for Macron and Lecornu. Markets so far have shown little reaction.

Sources: Al Jazeera Euronews CNBC CBS News

Other world headlines: Alberta vote, Gaza aid cut, Yemen

Facts

  • Alberta's nonbinding referendum: preliminary results show about 76% want to stay in Canada.
  • The UN World Food Programme cut Gaza aid by about a third for lack of funding, now reaching 1.1 million people, down from 1.6 million.
  • In Yemen, an attack on a security training center in Shabwa reportedly killed over 53 people; Houthis also fired missiles at Marib.
  • UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband warned firms off bidding on E1 settlement tenders in the West Bank. Japan launched the MMX probe toward Mars' moons.

Left view

Not enough distinct left/right coverage retrieved today; items come from a single Anadolu Agency briefing, so treat details as preliminary.

Right view

No right-leaning coverage retrieved on these items today.

Watch for

Gaza food aid shortfalls and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia feed regional escalation risk tied to the Iran war.

Sources: Anadolu Agency

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: up about 0.3% Tuesday. Dow: up about 1% (500+ points), led by 3M (+~6%). Nasdaq: fractionally lower, with chips weak (Yahoo Finance). Stocks rose after reports that mediators are working to bring the US and Iran together.
  • Oil: WTI fell 2.5% to about $101 after an eight-session rally of more than 20%; Brent was near $109 after touching its highest since mid-May.
  • Gas: AAA national average is $4.28, down from $4.34 a week ago and $4.48 a month ago, versus about $3.04 a year ago.
  • Rates: 10-year Treasury yield about 5.1%. The Fed hiked 25 bp in September (target 3.75%–4.00%) and meets Oct. 28; a hold is the base case, with a December hike priced as likely, per a broker's October preview (check current pricing).
  • Earnings & data: GM fell about 7% and GE Aerospace about 3.5%; Northrop rose 4.5%. Pending home sales dropped 7.3% in September versus a 0.4% decline expected. Headlines after hours said SpaceX beat on earnings with shares up 9%+ after hours, per secondary reports; Tesla reports Wednesday.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The PGA Tour is in its fall break after the Tour Championship (Scottie Scheffler won). On the DP World Tour, Eugenio Chacarra won the India Championship after switching to a broomstick putter.
  • Tennis: Almaty, Lyon and Brussels (ATP 250) and Ningbo (WTA 500) and Osaka (WTA 250) began this week. No results retrieved yet.
  • Squash: The $82,000 Venus ABC Open (PSA Copper) starts in Karachi Oct. 21–25, led by Curtis Malik (England) and Lucy Turmel (England), with Pakistan's Asim Khan seeded eighth.
  • WWE: Raw saw Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn clash ahead of Crown Jewel, Chad Gable retain the Intercontinental title over Dragon Lee and Rey Mysterio, and Bayley challenge Lyra Valkyria to a No DQ match.
  • Hockey: Rantanen had a hat trick including the OT winner for Boston at Dallas; Celebrini scored the OT winner for San Jose at Montreal; Bouchard's OT goal won it for Minnesota in Edmonton; DeBrincat hit 300 career goals in a Detroit comeback at Seattle.
  • Soccer: Premier League table (as of Oct. 19): Man City 21, Arsenal 18, Brighton 16, Chelsea 13, Liverpool 12. Tottenham beat Coventry 3-1 in a cup match.
  • Football: No reliable Week 7 results retrieved this morning; skipping rather than guessing.

item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Trump's approval hits new lows as Democrats lead the midterm ballot

Facts

  • Three new polls put Trump's approval at 33% (Washington Post-ABC-Ipsos), 34% (NBC) and 36% (Fox News), each reported as a record low or near it, per Axios.
  • Democrats lead the generic House ballot by 8 (Post), 9 (Fox) and 10 (NBC) points among registered voters.
  • Trump rallied in Kansas for Sen. Roger Marshall, calling the race close and some polls rigged; early voting opened Monday in Texas, parts of Florida, Colorado and Alaska.
  • Marquee races include Paxton vs. Talarico (TX), Rogers vs. El-Sayed (MI), and Collins vs. Jackson (ME).

Left view

The Washington Post and Axios frame the numbers as a clear Democratic edge and a GOP in damage-control mode; Democrats such as Hakeem Jeffries say they have momentum, and a CNBC piece argues the GOP's billion-dollar spending push is not moving numbers.

Right view

Fox News's coverage leads with Trump and Vance on the trail, Speaker Johnson's warnings about Democratic policy, DOJ voter-fraud charges in California, and Democratic controversies (El-Sayed, Omar, Khanna); Republicans argue polls understate their turnout.

Watch for

Forecasters will watch whether early-vote turnout tracks the polls; a gap this wide, if it holds, points to Democratic House gains and a competitive Senate map. Midterms are Nov 3.

Sources: Axios Washington Post Fox News CNBC

Trump waives Russia sanctions in a diesel deal; Putin floats a Trump-Xi summit

Facts

  • Trump suspended newly due Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, tied to a deal for Russian diesel: about 300,000 tons now and 4.5 million tons from November, per The Week. He called it a very good decision.
  • Zelenskyy called the move wrong and said it lets Putin kill more Ukrainians; Trump has also criticized Zelenskyy over Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries.
  • The WSJ reports Putin proposed a summit next month with Trump and Xi on ending the Ukraine war; Trump said he would meet them.
  • Senators of both parties, including Republicans Collins and Curtis, objected, per The Week and the Post.

Left view

The Washington Post reports bipartisan outrage. The Atlantic's Anne Applebaum and the FT's Edward Luce argue the policy consistently favors Moscow and amounts to pressuring Ukraine toward capitulation; The Bulwark says the diesel spike stems from the Iran war, not Ukraine.

Right view

Right-leaning criticism is notable: the WSJ editorial board called the move a moral and strategic mistake that funds Russia's war, and National Review's Andrew McCarthy called the diesel rationale a fraud because the US is a top oil exporter. Defenders inside the administration frame it as lowering fuel prices before the election; I saw little pro-waiver commentary in major outlets.

Watch for

Watch for congressional pushback on sanctions authority, Russian revenue and diesel prices, Ukraine's access to US intelligence and Starshield (reportedly throttled), and whether a three-way summit is actually scheduled.

Sources: The Week CNBC Washington Post The Hill Times of Israel

Iran war in its eighth month: Hormuz proposal stalls as Lavrov visits Tehran

Facts

  • Iran says its offer of a seven-day ceasefire and phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz remains open, conditional on the US lifting its naval blockade and sanctions; Trump rejected it last month.
  • Vance now says the US wants a meaningful cut to Iran's enrichment capacity, which some experts read as softer than earlier demands, per Al Jazeera.
  • Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov traveled to Tehran; Iran's IRGC said a tanker hit a mine in the southern Strait; UK forces counted 10 attacks on shipping near Hormuz last week.
  • Kpler data show non-Iranian Gulf oil flows at over 81% of pre-war levels in September.

Left view

Al Jazeera and other left-leaning and international outlets stress that Iran's priorities are the blockade, sanctions and frozen assets, that talks have broken down after US strikes, and that the war's costs fall on shipping and energy prices.

Right view

Administration allies, including Rubio (via the Times of Israel liveblog), argue the Iranian regime is the main obstacle to regional peace; Trump says the war ends the nice way or the not-so-nice way. Right-leaning commentary was thin in my search today.

Watch for

Analysts see oil staying near $100 while Hormuz is contested; a deal on the seven-day framework would likely knock prices down quickly, while further tanker attacks push gas and inflation higher.

Sources: Al Jazeera Times of Israel

Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia keep oil near $100

Facts

  • Houthis claim attacks on Saudi airports and Aramco facilities; Brent topped $109 on Sunday per CNBC, and US embassies in the region issued security alerts.
  • Saudi Arabia postponed an investor conference.
  • WTI was near $104 intraday Monday after the Houthi news, then futures settled lower (about $98) after the Russia sanctions waiver, per TheStreet and BBN Times.
  • NPR and Al Jazeera report fires, injuries and Saudi security alerts from the strikes.

Left view

NPR and Time emphasize the humanitarian and civilian toll in Saudi Arabia and Yemen and the widening of the Iran-linked conflict.

Right view

Right-leaning outlets frame the Houthis as Iran's proxies, which supports the case for pressure on Tehran. I did not retrieve specific right-leaning pieces on this today, so treat that as the typical framing, not a citation.

Watch for

Further hits on Saudi export infrastructure would push Brent higher; the Russian diesel volumes are small against US demand, so analysts do not expect a big pump-price relief from them.

Sources: CNBC NPR Al Jazeera

Israel heads to Oct. 27 election as Gaza ceasefire frays

Facts

  • Netanyahu told Israel's enemies not to test the country during an airbase visit; Benny Gantz withdrew from the race, and Eisenkot and Lapid called Netanyahu's security doctrine hollow.
  • The IDF says weekend strikes killed three Hamas operatives it called ceasefire violators; the UN World Food Programme will end monthly aid to 500,000 Gazans for lack of funding.
  • Settler attacks during the olive harvest led to 8 to 10 arrests; an Israeli man was shot dead near Eizariya.

Left view

Opposition leaders and international outlets focus on the security record, ceasefire violations, the aid cut and West Bank settler violence.

Right view

Pro-government framing, as in the Times of Israel's coverage of Netanyahu's remarks and Rubio's, centers on deterrence against Iran and on enforcing the ceasefire against Hamas. I only retrieved one main source here, so the left/right split is thin.

Watch for

The Oct. 27 vote and a post-election Gaza stabilization force (Moroccan troops reportedly training) are the next markers; Iran escalation is the main tail risk.

Sources: Times of Israel

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: closed Monday at 7,690.73 (+0.41%), roughly 2% below its early-October record. Dow: 51,966.03 (-0.07%). Nasdaq: 26,430.89 (+1.11%) as tech rebounded from last week's AI-spending selloff (BBN Times, TheStreet).
  • Oil: Brent topped $109 Sunday on Houthi attacks; US crude settled near $98 Monday after the Russia sanctions waiver (CNBC, BBN Times).
  • Gas: AAA national average $4.28, down from $4.34 a week ago and $4.48 a month ago, but about $1.25 above a year ago.
  • Rates: 10-year Treasury yield about 5.14%; the 30-year mortgage averaged 7.40% last week, near a three-year high, and homebuilder sentiment is at its lowest since 2012.
  • Earnings: GE Aerospace Tuesday morning; Netflix and SpaceX after the close; Tesla, Meta, IBM and Texas Instruments Wednesday.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Coverage was thin today; I found no confirmed weekend PGA Tour result. Last confirmed: Yin won LPGA Shanghai by a stroke over Choi (ESPN).
  • Tennis: Race to the ATP Finals: Zverev, Alcaraz and Shelton are in; Sinner is out with a knee injury. Cobolli, Medvedev, Tiafoe, Fils and Jodar hold the five open spots, with Djokovic seventh and playing a Basel wild card (Last Word on Sports).
  • Squash: No fresh PSA results found today; the 2026-27 PSA season is under way.
  • WWE: Raw (Oct 12): Chad Gable retained the Intercontinental title over Rey Fenix, and Carmelo Hayes joined The 946 in attacking The Bloodline (Fightful).
  • Hockey: Kaprizov scored his league-leading 10th as the Wild edged the Blue Jackets; Rangers beat the Ducks behind 29 saves from Garand; Michkov scored twice as the Flyers held off the Avalanche (NHL.com).
